messages:
Quentin Harris: trying to lock the field list for schema v1 today so I can stop bikeshedding in PR review 😅. current draft is here: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/PD/model-metadata-schema-v1

Quentin Harris: main open q: which fields are REQUIRED vs OPTIONAL (and which are internal-only). can folks weigh in? I’m proposing we keep required minimal to unblock backfill, but PM wants strong guarantees for customers.

Dylan Brooks: thx. +1 on minimal required. if we make half the world required we’ll end up with garbage placeholders just to pass validation.

Dylan Brooks: can we define required = needed to route/serve correctly + needed to explain breaking behavior to customers, and optional = “nice to have metadata / provenance details”.

Michael Nguyen: from migration side: if we mark too much required, backfill script will either (a) fail on most of catalog, or (b) we’ll fill "unknown" everywhere. neither is great.

Jada Williams: workflow angle: we can make some fields “required for publish” (customer-visible release note) even if they’re not required to exist in the registry record on day 1.

Quentin Harris: that’s a good split: required_for_record vs required_for_publish.

Jordan Lee: careful: validation rules in registry need to be deterministic. if we’re doing “required for publish”, it needs to live in the release-note workflow service (draft->in_review->published) not the core schema validator.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: +1. also RBAC: internal-only fields shouldn’t be writable by everyone. if we mix internal fields into the same “required” set, we’ll end up forcing broad write perms.

Quentin Harris: ok. here’s what I’m currently thinking for REQUIRED at record level (per model version):
```
identity:
  model_id
  version_id
  display_name

serving:
  context_window_tokens
  max_output_tokens
  tokenizer_id
  architecture_family

compat:
  api_compatibility: [chat_completions, completions, embeddings, rerank]
  supports_streaming

provenance:
  source_type (open|licensed|customer_provided)

lifecycle:
  created_at
  status (active|deprecated|disabled)
```
Thoughts?

Dylan Brooks: display_name required? I’d make that optional with fallback to model_id. we’ve had internal models without marketing names.

Marissa Cole: (jumping in) from customer UX, display_name is the anchor in the catalog + release notes. if it’s missing, it becomes “rw-llama-2-70b-q4_2023-11-07” which is… not great.

Michael Nguyen: we can make display_name required but allow autogenerated at migration time (e.g. title-case model_id + “(legacy)”). but Marissa is right, customer UX will suffer.

Quentin Harris: ok. if we require display_name, can we allow it to be updated later w/ audit trail? (i.e., display_name isn’t immutable)

Jordan Lee: yes, but need audit event for any customer-visible field changes.

Connor O'Brien: re lifecycle: I need `deprecation` object to have at least `sunset_date` and `replacement_model` when status=deprecated. otherwise release eng has nothing to plan with.

Dylan Brooks: agree but conditional required. when status=deprecated, require sunset_date and replacement_model. if active, optional / null.

Quentin Harris: +1. adding conditional constraints.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: also `created_at` is redundant if version_id encodes date sometimes. but fine.

Michael Nguyen: provenance.source_type (open|licensed|customer_provided) is ok, but I’m not sure we can reliably fill it for all existing versions. we can do “open” for curated open models, but some older ones are “??”

Dylan Brooks: then it can’t be required at record level. make provenance optional but strongly recommended.

Marissa Cole: I’m ok w/ provenance optional at record creation, but required before we publish a changelog entry. customers will ask “where did this come from / what changed” esp enterprise.

Jada Williams: that maps cleanly to workflow gate: publish requires provenance.source_type + at least one stable identifier (e.g. upstream repo tag or vendor version). doesn’t have to be weights sha.

Quentin Harris: noted. moving provenance -> required_for_publish.

Jordan Lee: internal-only: we should explicitly tag internal fields and have an allowlist for what can flow into customer release notes. otherwise we will leak stuff in generated summaries.

Quentin Harris: yep. in the spec I added `visibility: public|internal` per field but it’s messy. alternative is a `public_changelog_fields` allowlist in generator.

Dylan Brooks: prefer allowlist in generator + schema comments. field-level visibility tends to rot.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: from auth: allowlist also easier to enforce (service checks) without tying into every editor UI.

Quentin Harris: ok.

Quentin Harris: question: do we need `quantization` required? (e.g. q4_k_m, fp16) and `precision`/`dtype`.

Michael Nguyen: please no. quantization is missing on a bunch of legacy versions. also some are “mixed” depending on hardware.

Connor O'Brien: but quantization can absolutely change latency + quality. customers will feel it.

Dylan Brooks: then put it in optional metadata, and in changelog it’s included if present. required_for_publish only if we’re actually changing quantization.

Jada Williams: that’s the nuance: required_for_publish on a per-change basis. workflow should require certain fields only if the change touches that area.

Jordan Lee: careful with “per-change required”. we can do this at changelog template level: if diff includes quantization.* then template must include compatibility + impact section. not “schema required”.

Quentin Harris: makes sense. so quantization optional. template logic enforces narrative.

Marissa Cole: for the release note taxonomy I’m drafting, we’ll have categories (perf, compat, behavior, deprecation). if quantization changes, it should always create a “behavior/perf” note with a clear callout.

Quentin Harris: cool.

Quentin Harris: also debating `context_window_tokens` required. I think yes because tooling + customers pin based on this.

Dylan Brooks: yes. required.

Michael Nguyen: yes.

Connor O'Brien: yes.

Jordan Lee: +1.

Quentin Harris: `tool/function calling compatibility` fields: `supports_tool_calls`, `supports_json_schema`, etc. required?

Dylan Brooks: I’d do required for chat models only. embeddings don’t care.

Quentin Harris: schema currently has `capabilities` object with booleans. if absent, we assume false. I’m nervous about assuming false when unknown.

Marissa Cole: from customer perspective, unknown should be explicit. “Not supported” is different from “not specified”.

Jordan Lee: we can model tri-state: true/false/unspecified. but adds complexity.

Jada Williams: compromise: require `capabilities` object present but allow fields null. then UI can render “—” vs “No”.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: nullability will complicate API clients a bit but manageable.

Dylan Brooks: I’d rather not introduce nulls everywhere. Can we have `capabilities_known: true/false`? if false, treat others as unknown.

Quentin Harris: interesting. `capabilities.known=true` then booleans must be present. `known=false` then omit.

Marissa Cole: works for UI + release notes.

Quentin Harris: ok adding that.

Michael Nguyen: pls also add a single `api_compatibility` enum list as you had. we can backfill that fairly easily and it drives routing.

Quentin Harris: yep.

Quentin Harris: last contentious one: `weights_hash` (sha256) / artifact digest. security wants it. do we require?

Jordan Lee: security will want tamper-evidence, but registry schema v1 doesn’t have to require hash to exist for every old model. For new onboarded models, we can require `artifact_digest`.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: +1. do not block legacy. but for new versions, require artifact_digest if source_type != customer_provided? actually customer_provided also should have digest if we store it.

Connor O'Brien: we can do “required for new records after cutoff date”. but that’s policy, not schema.

Dylan Brooks: let’s keep schema permissive and enforce policy in onboarding pipeline + review checklist.

Quentin Harris: ok.

Quentin Harris: action items:
- I’ll update draft Confluence + PR to split “record required” vs “publish required” sections.
- move provenance + artifact_digest to publish gate / onboarding policy
- keep context_window_tokens + api_compatibility required
- add conditional required deprecation fields when status=deprecated
- propose capabilities_known pattern

Quentin Harris: if anyone objects, pls reply today. trying to cut schema v1 by EOD so ENG-4922 can proceed.

Dylan Brooks: :thumbsup:

Michael Nguyen: :thumbsup: (and thank you for not making me backfill 80 fields)

Marissa Cole: :thumbsup: pls @ me on the updated spec; I want to make sure customer-facing fields are called out clearly.

Jordan Lee: :thumbsup: and make sure the changelog generator has an explicit public allowlist. I don’t want “vendor_internal_name” ending up in docs.

Quentin Harris: yep will do.

Connor O'Brien: also can we add an example record + example changelog entry in the Confluence page? would help release eng sanity check.

Quentin Harris: already have a stub example, will flesh out w/ one “active” and one “deprecated” version + show what gets rendered.

Jada Williams: pls include workflow states too (draft/in_review/published) even if high-level. it’ll help align expectations.

Quentin Harris: will add a section.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: +1 on examples. also include which roles can edit which fields (even a rough table).

Quentin Harris: ok adding a mini RBAC table w/ “editor/publisher” roles and field categories.

Dylan Brooks: let’s keep RBAC table as “proposed” so we don’t block schema on it.

Quentin Harris: yep, will mark as TBD / linked to ENG-4932.

(Quentin Harris edited) updated draft: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/PD/model-metadata-schema-v1#Required-vs-Publish-Gates

Marissa Cole: reading now

Marissa Cole: looks good. only nit: rename `display_name` to `public_name`? “display_name” implies internal UI too.

Quentin Harris: hmm. I’d rather not rename at this stage. can document semantics: customer-visible name.

Dylan Brooks: agree keep display_name.

Jordan Lee: naming is fine. semantics > perfect name.

Connor O'Brien: ok with display_name.

Quentin Harris: cool. shipping the update + moving discussion to PR comments if needed.
